section_item2_bakeReachability_FINDING.method: The publish image's LDT content is not the LDT checkout. Dockerfile.publish's final stage (lines 17-24) copies only /ldt/node_modules and /app/bakes; /app/bakes is produced by scripts/build-publish-bake-clis.mjs, which esbuild-bundles exactly four entrypoints (lines 27-32): nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts, nodeFacetBakeTier2ConformantCli.ts, parcelsPmtilesBakeCli.ts, nodeFacetPatchCadRollFromCadPropertyCli.ts. That graph was traced at SHA 3885efad by reading every module with git show (no checkout, no write to legacy-design-tools): 26 modules, 0 unresolved relative specifiers.

section_disagreements.severity: material -- changes what this pin bump can be claimed to accomplish
section_disagreements.dispatchText: '69de8fe6 is CTX-MIRROR. Production cortex-api-00754-feg is ALREADY built from it. So the serve projects the rail's own refused state while the bake, pinned to 301bb75a, does not write it. The bake is behind the serve on the exact field the zoning walk grades.'
section_disagreements.finding: The premise that the pin bump closes a bake/serve gap on 69de8fe6 is not supported. 69de8fe6 changes only artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelRecordCellRead.ts and structuralFactToFacetsWire.ts (plus their tests). Neither file is reachable from any of the four bake entrypoints, so neither is compiled into /app/bakes. Bumping the pin from 301bb75a to 3885efad does not change the bake's behaviour with respect to 69de8fe6 at all -- before or after, the bake does not contain that code. Whatever bake/serve disagreement exists on the refused state, this pin bump is not the lever that closes it; the refused state is written by the parcel-r5-zoning RAIL out of hauska-factory's own src (UPDATE_ZONING_CELLS_SQL, per the rescued config's header), not by the LDT bake.
section_disagreements.evidentiaryStandard: DEV_PROCESS 3.2a -- this correction quotes source and names files. Dockerfile.publish:17-24, scripts/build-publish-bake-clis.mjs:27-32, plus the 26-module trace and the repo-wide importer scan above.
section_disagreements.doesItChangeTheAction: No. The bump still proceeds, because 3885efad DOES reach the bake and adds recordRetirement to nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts, which is the honest justification for it. The pin comment will say that and will not repeat the 69de8fe6 claim.
section_disagreements.residualUncertainty: This is a static-reachability argument. It proves the code is not in the bundle. It does not prove that no bake/serve disagreement exists on the refused state by some other mechanism -- only that this pin does not address one.

section_item3_design.predicate: allowlist id -> the src/jobs module declaring JOB_ID === id -> the cli.mjs `cmd === "<command>"` branch that imports that module -> a `gcloud run jobs deploy` block in some cloudbuild*.yaml whose --args names that command. Same shape as the existing reachability test: two independently derived sources asked whether they agree.
section_item3_design.whyNotTheObviousPredicate: Matching the allowlist id against any --args= in any cloudbuild file would pass on DOCUMENTATION. cloudbuild.parcel-acquire-gis.yaml and cloudbuild.parcel-wave2.yaml carry commented `gcloud run jobs execute ... --args=<id>` example lines. A check satisfied by a comment is a fail-open of exactly the class this program hunts, so comment lines are stripped before parsing and only text inside a `gcloud run jobs deploy` block counts.
section_item3_design.knownIndirection: cloudbuild.publish.yaml deploys five jobs through a shell for-loop with --args=$$ARGS and a per-job case block. A deploy whose --args is a shell variable resolves to every literal assignment of that variable in the same file. This is an approximation and will be stated in the instrument's bypasses section.

section_item3_design.theSixAreNotExemptions: All six refuse --apply unless FACTORY_CLOUD=1 (p3-absence.mjs:53-54, purge-bastrop-orphans.mjs:89-90, parcel-value-history.mjs:258-259, s6-collision-remediate.mjs:171-172, vh-collision-remediate.mjs:170-171, owner-rail-collision-check.mjs:502-503, each refusing LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN). A read-only gcloud run jobs list confirms none of factory-p3-absence, factory-purge-bastrop-orphans, factory-parcel-value-history, factory-s6-collision-remediate, factory-vh-collision-remediate or factory-owner-rail-collision-check exists in hauska-prod-497015/us-east4. So all six are dispatchable, cloud-gated, and have nowhere to execute -- their --apply path cannot run anywhere. That is the A-120 class, six live instances of it, and calling them exemptions would be dishonest. Declared exemptions in this lane: 0.
section_item3_design.howTheTestStaysHonestWithoutBeingPermane: DEV_PROCESS 2.0 says a permanently-red gate is a dead gate. The repo already has the right idiom for this: ORPHANS_KNOWN in the existing test is a pinned quarantine, not an exemption. The new check pins the six as UNDEPLOYABLE_KNOWN with a written reason each, asserts deep-equality against that frozen set so the set cannot GROW unnoticed, and states in the file that shrinking it is the point.
section_item3_design.provingItCanFire: Required by the dispatch and by DEV_PROCESS 2.2. Will be demonstrated two ways: (a) in-file VIOLATION tests that run every time, and (b) the dispatch's own demonstration -- delete a real config from the working tree, show the suite go red, restore it, show it go green. Exit codes read from the process, never from a pipe (DEV_PROCESS 2.3).
